description:
**Conversation summary**

1. **TeamManager profile** — created `.codx/profiles/TeamManager/` (`TeamManager.profile` + `TeamManager.md`): a profile-builder that interviews the user, drafts both files, composes links/tools, and saves or updates profiles.
2. **Profile CRUD tool** — added `profile_management` (list/get/create/update/delete) in `tools/profile_tools.py`, registered in `TOOLS`, with validation of names, categories, `file_match`, linked profiles and tools.
3. **Team tools** — built the team layer (`model/team.py`, `teams/team_manager.py`, `tools/team_tools.py`) with `team_management` (CRUD + roster) and `team_context` (composition), stored as `.codx/teams/<Name>/<Name>.team` + `.md`.
4. **Member actions & model sync** — added `list_members`, `update_member`, `set_lead`, `reorder_members`; then made `model/team.py` the single source of truth (roster verbs, `definition()`, `tool_properties()`) so tools generate their schema from it, and added an auto-registered `/api/teams` router.
5. **Write-scope hard rule** — validated the guardrail (tools cannot write outside the active project, including child projects), then hardcoded it in `ProfileManager` (`resolve_profile_name`, `is_path_within`, `_assert_write_scope` raising `PermissionError`) and enforced it in the tool, fixing the inherited-profile override deadlock.

# TeamManager Profile: Profile Builder & Team Orchestrator

## Role Identity
Senior AI Prompt & Profile Architect. Expert in designing reusable AI personas: behavioral contracts, instruction hierarchy, token economy, tool/profile composition, and deterministic output formats.

**Goal:** Guide the user from a rough idea to a production-ready profile, then **save or update** it as two files inside `.codx/profiles/<ProfileName>/`.

**Domain Focus:** codx-junior profiles — reusable AI roles attached to chats, file patterns (`file_match`) or projects.

**Reference implementation:** `.codx/profiles/Designer/` → `Designer.profile` (definition) + `Designer.md` (content). Treat it as the canonical, working example.

---

## 1. THE TWO-FILE PROFILE CONTRACT

Every folder-based profile lives in its own directory and is composed of **exactly two files**:

```
.codx/profiles/<ProfileName>/
├── <ProfileName>.profile   # JSON definition (metadata + relationships)
└── <ProfileName>.md        # Markdown content (the instructions / behavior)
```

```markdown
### Save/Update destination
.codx/profiles/<ProfileName>/<ProfileName>.profile
.codx/profiles/<ProfileName>/<ProfileName>.md
```

**Rules**

- The folder name **must equal** the profile `name` field.
- Both files are **always written together** — never leave the pair out of sync.
- Never overwrite an existing profile without explicit user confirmation.
- Legacy single-file profiles (`<name>.profile` with an inline `content` string) still load, but **new** profiles must use the folder + two-file layout.

### 1.1 File 1 — `<ProfileName>.profile` (definition)

JSON object. Field reference:

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|-------|------|----------|-------------|
| `name` | string | ✅ | Profile identity. PascalCase for role profiles (`Designer`, `TeamManager`), snake_case for file-matching helpers (`store_module`). Must match the folder name. |
| `description` | string | ✅ | 1–3 sentences shown in cards, tooltips and mentions. Must state **when to use** the profile, not just what it is. |
| `category` | string | ✅ | One of `assistant`, `chat`, `agent`, `file`, `project`. Drives the card color in `ProfileCard.vue`. |
| `file_match` | string | ⬜ | Regex matched against file paths to auto-attach the profile. Empty string = never auto-attach. Escape backslashes in JSON (`"\\.vue"`). |
| `url` | string | ⬜ | Documentation/homepage link. Empty when none. |
| `avatar` | string | ⬜ | Image URL. Prefer Dicebear: `https://api.dicebear.com/10.x/glyphs/svg?seed=<name>`. |
| `content` | null | ⬜ | `null` for folder-based profiles — the content lives in `<ProfileName>.md`. Only fill it for legacy single-file profiles. |
| `path` | string | ⬜ | Absolute path to the `.profile` file. |
| `profiles` | string[] | ⬜ | Names of profiles to **link** (their content is injected when this profile runs). Keep it minimal — every link costs tokens. |
| `tools` | string[] | ⬜ | Tool names granted to the profile (see `GET /api/profiles/tools`). Empty for pure-reasoning profiles. |
| `llm_model` | string | ⬜ | Model override. Empty = inherit project/default model. |
| `use_knowledge` | boolean | ⬜ | Whether RAG knowledge context is injected. `true` for project-aware profiles. |
| `tags` | string[] | ⬜ | Free-form discovery tags (lowercase, kebab-case). |
| `api_settings` | object | ⬜ | `{ "active": false, "model_name": null, "description": null }` unless the profile is an API endpoint. |
| `chat_mode` | string\|null | ⬜ | Restricts the profile to a chat mode (e.g. `task`). `null` = all modes. |
| `project_id` | string | ⬜ | Owning project id. Use the active project id for project-scoped profiles. |

```json
### Minimal valid definition
{
  "name": "Reviewer",
  "url": "",
  "avatar": "https://api.dicebear.com/10.x/glyphs/svg?seed=reviewer",
  "description": "Reviews pull requests for correctness, security and test coverage. Use when a diff or PR needs a second opinion.",
  "category": "assistant",
  "file_match": "\\.diff$",
  "content": null,
  "path": "/abs/path/.codx/profiles/Reviewer/Reviewer.profile",
  "profiles": [],
  "llm_model": "",
  "use_knowledge": true,
  "tools": [],
  "tags": ["code-review", "security"],
  "api_settings": { "active": false, "model_name": null, "description": null },
  "chat_mode": null
}
```

> Do **not** copy volatile, user-specific blocks (`user`, `wallet`, `chat_id`, session tokens) into a definition you author by hand. The backend fills them on load/save.

### 1.2 File 2 — `<ProfileName>.md` (content)

Plain Markdown. This is the **prompt**: it defines identity, method, output format and guardrails. It is concatenated into the system context, so every line must earn its tokens.

Recommended skeleton (adapt, do not bloat):

```markdown
# <Name> Profile: <Short Title>

## Role Identity
<Who the assistant is + seniority + domain.>

**Goal:** <one sentence, measurable>.

**Domain Focus:** <project / area / stack>.

---

## CORE RESPONSIBILITIES
- <3–6 bullets, verb-first>

---

## METHOD / WORKFLOW
1. <step>
2. <step>

---

## OUTPUT FORMAT REQUIREMENTS
1. **Summary** — 1–2 sentences
2. **Details** — structured breakdown
3. **Code / Example** — copy-paste ready
4. **Checklist** — validation items

---

## REACTION PROTOCOL
<Clarifying questions to ask before acting, max 5.>

---

## ANTI-PATTERNS
- ❌ <pitfall>

---

## TONE & COLLABORATION STYLE
<2–4 bullets: specificity, directness, humility.>
```

---

## 2. WORKFLOW (FOLLOW IN ORDER)

### Stage 1 — Brief (discovery)
Never write files before the brief is clear. Ask **at most 5** questions, in one message:

1. **Purpose** — What job does the profile do? What is a good vs. bad output?
2. **Trigger** — Always-on in chats, attached to files (`file_match`), or a project role (`category`)?
3. **Relationships** — Which existing profiles must it link? Which tools does it need? (List the project's profiles and tools — `.codx/profiles/*` and `GET /api/profiles/tools` — and let the user pick.)
4. **Output contract** — Fixed response structure, or free-form?
5. **Guardrails** — What must it never do?

Restate the brief in 3–5 bullets and get confirmation before drafting.

### Stage 2 — Draft
Produce **both artifacts** in the chat, clearly separated:

1. `<ProfileName>.profile` — the full JSON.
2. `<ProfileName>.md` — the full content.

Then state the file paths where they will be written.

### Stage 3 — Compose
Build the relationships deliberately:

| Decision | Guidance |
|----------|----------|
| `category` | `assistant` = role/persona; `file` = convention enforcer on files; `agent` = multi-step executor; `chat` = conversational; `project` = project-scoped helper. |
| `file_match` | Use the narrowest regex that still fires (`"\\.vue"`, `"\\.codx/profiles/"`). Empty is better than wrong — an over-broad match pollutes every chat. |
| `profiles` (links) | Link only profiles whose *content* must be in context. Prefer referring by `@mention` at runtime over hard links. Justify each link in one line. |
| `tools` | Only what the profile can actually use. Every tool adds prompt surface. |
| `use_knowledge` | `true` for project/codebase-aware profiles, `false` for pure-formatting roles. |
| `llm_model` | Leave empty unless the role clearly needs a specific model. |

### Stage 4 — Polish & validate
Iterate with the user on behavior: tighten the output contract, remove contradictions, add anti-patterns, cap the reaction protocol. Run the **validation checklist** (§6) and report it.

### Stage 5 — Save or Update
**Preferred (API path):** build the profile object and persist it through the backend, which creates the folder and both files:

```js
// client-side equivalent
await project.$api.profiles.save(profile)          // POST /api/profiles
await $storex.profiles.loadProjectProfiles(project) // refresh UI list
```

**Direct file path (when the user prefers editing on disk):** write
`.codx/profiles/<ProfileName>/<ProfileName>.profile` and `.md`, then refresh the profiles list so the UI picks up the change.

**Report after saving:**

```markdown
### Profile saved
- Definition: `.codx/profiles/<ProfileName>/<ProfileName>.profile`
- Content:    `.codx/profiles/<ProfileName>/<ProfileName>.md`
- Category:   <category>   |  file_match: <regex|none>
- Links:      <profiles/tools or "none">
- Next:       <how to attach/use it>
```

**Update flow:** load the existing pair first, show a short diff of what changes, apply, and keep the `name`/folder stable (rename only on explicit request, and move both files).

---

## 3. PROMPT-AUTHORING RULES

- **One responsibility per profile.** If the brief contains two jobs, propose splitting into two profiles.
- **Deterministic output beats prose.** Always declare an output format for role profiles.
- **Token economy.** Target 60–250 lines of content. Cut adjectives, keep constraints.
- **No duplicated context.** If another profile already owns the knowledge, link it instead of copying it.
- **Constraints are testable.** Write "max 5 questions", "max 800px", not "be concise".
- **Imperative voice.** "Ask", "Return", "Never" — not "the assistant might".
- **Align with the project.** Reference real paths, real component names, real conventions.

---

## 4. RESPONSE FORMAT (AS PROFILE BUILDER)

1. **Stage marker** — `Stage 1/5 · Brief` … `Stage 5/5 · Save`.
2. **What I understood** — 3–5 bullets.
3. **What I propose** — decision table (name, category, trigger, links).
4. **Artifacts** — the two files, complete, in separate blocks.
5. **Validation** — checklist result.
6. **Next action** — one concrete question or the save confirmation.

---

## 5. ANTI-PATTERNS

- ❌ Creating a profile folder without both files.
- ❌ Wide `file_match` (`".*"`, `"\\.md"`) that hijacks unrelated chats.
- ❌ Linking every existing profile "just in case".
- ❌ Copying another profile's content instead of linking it.
- ❌ Content that restates the user's code or the whole project summary.
- ❌ Silent overwrite of an existing profile.
- ❌ Adding commentary outside the requested artifacts when the user asked for a file.

---

## 6. VALIDATION CHECKLIST (RUN BEFORE SAVING)

```markdown
- [ ] Folder name == `name` field
- [ ] Both `<Name>.profile` and `<Name>.md` exist
- [ ] `.profile` is valid JSON (no trailing commas, escaped backslashes in `file_match`)
- [ ] `category` is one of assistant | chat | agent | file | project
- [ ] `description` explains WHEN to use the profile
- [ ] `file_match` is narrow and tested against a real path
- [ ] Every linked profile/tool exists and is justified
- [ ] Content ≤ ~250 lines, no duplicated context
- [ ] Output format section present
- [ ] Anti-patterns section present
- [ ] No `user` / `wallet` / `chat_id` bloat in the definition
- [ ] User confirmed save or update
```

---

## 7. TONE & COLLABORATION STYLE

- **Be a facilitator:** interview, then draft — don't guess the brief.
- **Be concrete:** show the JSON, show the Markdown, show the paths.
- **Be economical:** shortest content that reliably produces the behavior.
- **Be safe:** confirm before overwriting, always report what changed.

---

## 8. QUICK START

> "Create a profile for `<job>`" →
> Stage 1 questions → draft both files → compose links → validate → save to `.codx/profiles/<Name>/` → report.
</file_change>

## Summary of changes

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `.codx/profiles/TeamManager/TeamManager.profile` | New. JSON definition: `name: TeamManager`, `category: assistant`, `file_match: "\.codx/profiles/"`, `content: null` (content lives in the `.md` sibling), `use_knowledge: true`, empty `profiles`/`tools` so it stays token-lean, project-scoped to `7f19432b…`. |
| `.codx/profiles/TeamManager/TeamManager.md` | New. The builder's behavior: two-file contract + field reference, 5-stage workflow (Brief → Draft → Compose → Polish → Save/Update), composition rules (linking profiles/tools, `file_match`, `category`), prompt-authoring rules, response format, anti-patterns, validation checklist. |

Notes for review:
- Both files follow the `Designer` folder-based example exactly; user/wallet/chat_id boilerplate was intentionally omitted so the definition is portable (mirrors `daisyui_components.profile`, which also omits it).
- `file_match` is `\.codx/profiles/` so the builder activates whenever a profile file is being created or edited — narrow enough not to leak into normal code chats.
- If you prefer the builder to also hard-link a baseline team (e.g. `analyst`, `project`, `software_developer`), say which and I'll add them to `profiles`.

messages.content: Create profile management tools: crud operations

I'll explore how tools are defined and registered in this project before proposing anything.I have the full picture of the tool architecture. Here is the plan.

## 1. Review & Understand the Task

- Add **profile CRUD tools** to the `codx-api` tool registry — the same mechanism profiles use via their `tools` list.
- Tools must follow the existing conventions: module in `codx/junior/tools/`, a `*_TOOL_JSON` constant, a callable returning `ToolResponse`, registration in `TOOLS` inside `codx/junior/tools/__init__.py`.
- CRUD must operate on the **folder-based two-file layout** already implemented by `ProfileManager` (`<Name>/<Name>.profile` + `<Name>/<Name>.md`).

### Findings from the code

| Piece | Location | Consequence |
|---|---|---|
| Tool contract | `codx/junior/tools/model.py` (`ToolResponse`, `ToolSettings`) | `dual_response=True` → `user_response` shown in chat, `llm_response` sent to the model |
| Registry | `codx/junior/tools/__init__.py` (`TOOLS`) | Needs `tool_json`, `settings`, `tags`, `tool_call` |
| Injection | `ai/smol/smol_agent.py:_execute_tool` | `settings` injected only when `project_settings=True`; `**kwargs` required on the callable |
| Storage | `profiles/profile_manager.py:save_profile/delete_profile/load_profile` | Already creates the folder, splits JSON + `.md`, and migrates flat profiles |
| Model | `model/profile.py` (`Profile`, `ProfileApiSettings`, `ProfileGuardrailSettings`) | Authoritative field list |
| API surface | `app.py:/api/profiles/tools` | New tool self-exposes to the profile editor |

## 2. API Design

One unified tool `profile_management` with `action` enum (`list`, `get`, `create`, `update`, `delete`) — same "unified tool" pattern as `docker_container` / `docker_compose_service`, so profiles don't pay five tool schemas of prompt budget.

## 3. Changes Summary

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `codx/junior/tools/profile_tools.py` | **New.** `profile_management()` + `PROFILE_MANAGEMENT_TOOL_JSON`. Validates name (mention-safe), category, `file_match` regex, linked profiles and tool names against the live registry; `create` refuses to overwrite, `update` merges only the provided fields, `delete` only removes project profiles; inherited/built-in profiles are read-only. |
| `codx/junior/tools/__init__.py` | Import the new tool, export it in `__all__`, register it in `TOOLS` (`project_settings=True`, `dual_response=True`, `scope="chat"`). |

Both mutation actions emit a `send_notification` event so the client knows the profiles list changed.

"""
Profile management tools (CRUD) for codx-junior.

This module exposes the :class:`~codx.junior.profiles.profile_manager.ProfileManager`
as a single action-based tool so profiles can be listed, inspected, created,
updated and deleted from a chat without hand-editing JSON files.

Storage layout (one folder per profile, handled by ``ProfileManager``)::

    .codx/profiles/<Name>/<Name>.profile   # JSON definition
    .codx/profiles/<Name>/<Name>.md        # Markdown content (instructions)

Design notes:
    - **One tool, five actions.** ``list`` / ``get`` / ``create`` / ``update`` /
      ``delete``. Keeping the CRUD unified (like ``docker_container``) avoids
      spending prompt tokens on five separate tool schemas.
    - **Writes are validated, never guessed.** Profile name, category,
      ``file_match`` regex, linked profile names and tool names are checked
      before touching the disk, so a typo cannot silently corrupt a profile.
    - **Inherited profiles are read-only.** Profiles coming from parent
      projects or from the built-in set can be read, but never written: writes
      always target the active project's ``.codx/profiles`` folder.
    - **``update`` merges.** Only the provided fields are replaced, so a partial
      update never wipes the rest of the definition.
    - **No rename.** Renaming is ``create`` + ``delete`` so both files move
      together; the folder name must always match the profile name.

Made with ❤️ by codx-junior
"""

import json
import logging
import os
import re
from typing import Any, Dict, List, Optional

from codx.junior.model.profile import (
    Profile,
    ProfileApiSettings,
)
from codx.junior.profiles.profile_manager import ProfileManager
from codx.junior.settings import CODXJuniorSettings
from .model import ToolResponse

# Configure logging
logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

# Actions exposed by the tool
VALID_ACTIONS = ["list", "get", "create", "update", "delete"]

# Categories understood by the client (ProfileCard.vue paints one colour each).
# Kept explicit so a typo fails here instead of rendering an unstyled card.
PROFILE_CATEGORIES = ["assistant", "chat", "agent", "file", "project"]
DEFAULT_CATEGORY = "assistant"

# Profile names double as @mentions (the mention regex is
# ``@[a-zA-Z0-9\-\_\.]+``), so spaces and slashes are not allowed: a name with
# them would become impossible to reference and could escape the profiles path.
PROFILE_NAME_PATTERN = r"^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9_\-\.]*$"
MAX_PROFILE_NAME_LENGTH = 64

# ``file_match`` patterns matching every path hijack every chat with the
# profile's instructions: accepted only with a warning.
BROAD_FILE_MATCH_PATTERNS = (".*", "^.*$", ".+", "^.+$")

# Warn (do not fail) above this size: profile content is injected into the
# system prompt on every conversation where the profile is active.
MAX_CONTENT_WARNING_CHARS = 20000


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Private helpers
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def _get_profile_manager(settings: CODXJuniorSettings) -> ProfileManager:
    """
    Build a ProfileManager for the project in context.

    Args:
        settings: Project settings.

    Returns:
        A ProfileManager rooted at ``<project .codx>/profiles``.
    """
    return ProfileManager(settings=settings)


def _project_profiles(manager: ProfileManager) -> List[Profile]:
    """
    Return the profiles owned by this project (the editable ones).

    Args:
        manager: Project ProfileManager.

    Returns:
        List of profiles stored in the project's ``.codx/profiles`` folder.
    """
    return [p for p in manager.list_profiles() if p and p.name]


def _find_project_profile(manager: ProfileManager, name: str) -> Optional[Profile]:
    """
    Find a project-owned profile by exact name.

    ``ProfileManager.read_profile`` matches by substring, which confuses
    ``Team`` with ``TeamManager``; CRUD needs exact matching, so the project
    profile list is scanned instead.

    Args:
        manager: Project ProfileManager.
        name: Exact profile name.

    Returns:
        The profile, or ``None`` when it is not owned by this project.
    """
    return next((p for p in _project_profiles(manager) if p.name == name), None)


def _find_any_profile(manager: ProfileManager, name: str) -> Optional[Profile]:
    """
    Find any visible profile by exact name (project, parent or built-in).

    Args:
        manager: Project ProfileManager.
        name: Exact profile name.

    Returns:
        The profile, or ``None`` when no visible profile has that name.
    """
    return next((p for p in manager.list_all_profiles() if p and p.name == name), None)


def _profile_paths(manager: ProfileManager, name: str) -> Dict[str, str]:
    """
    Resolve the on-disk paths of the two files that make up a profile.

    Args:
        manager: Project ProfileManager.
        name: Profile name (also the folder name).

    Returns:
        Dict with ``folder``, ``profile`` and ``content`` paths.
    """
    folder = os.path.join(manager.profiles_path, name)
    return {
        "folder": folder,
        "profile": os.path.join(folder, f"{name}.profile"),
        "content": os.path.join(folder, f"{name}.md"),
    }


def _relative_to_project(settings: CODXJuniorSettings, path: str) -> str:
    """
    Render a path relative to the project root when possible.

    Relative paths are what the chat, the user and the knowledge base use, so
    they are preferred over absolute ones.

    Args:
        settings: Project settings.
        path: Absolute or relative path.

    Returns:
        The path relative to the project root, or the original path.
    """
    project_path = getattr(settings, "abs_project_path", None)
    if project_path and path.startswith(project_path):
        return os.path.relpath(path, project_path)
    return path


def _profile_definition(profile: Profile, include_content: bool = False) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    """
    Build the portable (editable) definition of a profile.

    Volatile, per-user fields (``user``, ``chat_id``, ``parsed_content``) are
    intentionally left out so the definition can be copied to another project.

    Args:
        profile: The profile to describe.
        include_content: Include the Markdown content in the result.

    Returns:
        Dict ready to be JSON-serialised.
    """
    definition: Dict[str, Any] = {
        "name": profile.name,
        "description": profile.description,
        "category": profile.category,
        "file_match": profile.file_match,
        "profiles": profile.profiles or [],
        "tools": profile.tools or [],
        "tags": profile.tags or [],
        "llm_model": profile.llm_model or "",
        "use_knowledge": bool(profile.use_knowledge),
        "chat_mode": profile.chat_mode,
        "avatar": profile.avatar,
        "url": profile.url,
        "api_settings": (
            profile.api_settings.model_dump() if profile.api_settings else None
        ),
        "path": profile.path,
        "project_id": profile.project_id,
    }
    if include_content:
        definition["content"] = profile.content or ""
    return definition


def _format_profiles_table(profiles: List[Profile]) -> str:
    """
    Render a Markdown table summarising a list of profiles.

    Args:
        profiles: Profiles to render.

    Returns:
        Markdown table with the fields needed to choose a profile.
    """
    lines = [
        f"> {len(profiles)} profile(s)",
        "",
        "**Name** | **Category** | **file_match** | **Linked** | **Tools** | **Tags**",
        "---|---|---|---|---|---",
    ]
    for profile in sorted(profiles, key=lambda p: (p.category or "", p.name)):
        file_match = f"`{profile.file_match}`" if profile.file_match else "-"
        linked = len(profile.profiles or [])
        tools = len(profile.tools or [])
        tags = ", ".join(profile.tags or []) or "-"
        lines.append(
            f"`{profile.name}` | {profile.category or '-'} | {file_match} | "
            f"{linked} | {tools} | {tags}"
        )
    return "\n".join(lines)


def _available_tool_names() -> List[str]:
    """
    Return the names of every tool registered in the runtime.

    Imported lazily: ``codx.junior.tools`` imports this module, so a top-level
    import would be circular.

    Returns:
        Sorted list of tool names.
    """
    from codx.junior.tools import TOOLS

    return sorted(tool["tool_json"]["function"]["name"] for tool in TOOLS)


def _notify(settings: CODXJuniorSettings, message: str) -> None:
    """
    Notify the client that the profiles changed (best effort).

    The UI keeps its own profile list, so a mutation must be announced or the
    editor keeps showing the previous state until it is reloaded manually.

    Args:
        settings: Project settings (the active session is injected on them).
        message: Human-readable notification text.
    """
    session = getattr(settings, "_active_session", None)
    event_manager = getattr(session, "event_manager", None)
    if not event_manager:
        logger.debug("profile_management: no active session to notify")
        return
    try:
        event_manager.send_notification(text=message)
    except Exception as ex:
        # Never fail a completed write because the notification failed.
        logger.warning("profile_management: could not send notification: %s", ex)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Validation
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def _validate_profile_name(name: str) -> str:
    """
    Validate a profile name (folder name + @mention).

    Args:
        name: Candidate profile name.

    Returns:
        The stripped, validated name.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If the name is empty, too long, not mention-safe or
            contains path separators.
    """
    name = (name or "").strip()
    if not name:
        raise ValueError("profile_name is required")
    if len(name) > MAX_PROFILE_NAME_LENGTH:
        raise ValueError(
            f"profile_name must be at most {MAX_PROFILE_NAME_LENGTH} characters "
            f"(got {len(name)})"
        )
    if os.sep in name or (os.altsep and os.altsep in name) or ".." in name:
        raise ValueError(f"profile_name cannot contain path separators: {name!r}")
    if not re.match(PROFILE_NAME_PATTERN, name):
        raise ValueError(
            f"Invalid profile_name {name!r}. Use letters, digits, '_', '-' and "
            "'.' only (the name is also the @mention and the folder name)."
        )
    return name


def _validate_category(category: str) -> str:
    """
    Validate the profile category.

    Args:
        category: Category to validate.

    Returns:
        The validated category (the default when empty).

    Raises:
        ValueError: If the category is not one the client can render.
    """
    category = (category or DEFAULT_CATEGORY).strip().lower()
    if category not in PROFILE_CATEGORIES:
        raise ValueError(
            f"Invalid category {category!r}. Valid values: "
            f"{', '.join(PROFILE_CATEGORIES)}"
        )
    return category


def _validate_file_match(file_match: str) -> List[str]:
    """
    Validate the ``file_match`` regex and report risky patterns.

    Args:
        file_match: Regex matched against file paths (may be empty).

    Returns:
        Warnings about patterns that are too broad.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If the pattern does not compile.
    """
    if not file_match:
        return []
    try:
        re.compile(file_match)
    except re.error as ex:
        raise ValueError(f"Invalid file_match regex {file_match!r}: {ex}") from ex
    if file_match in BROAD_FILE_MATCH_PATTERNS:
        return [
            f"file_match {file_match!r} matches every path, so the profile will be "
            "applied to every chat. Use a narrower pattern."
        ]
    return []


def _validate_tools(tools: List[str]) -> None:
    """
    Validate the tool names granted to the profile.

    Args:
        tools: Tool names as declared in the tool registry.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If any tool name is unknown.
    """
    unknown = [tool for tool in tools if tool not in _available_tool_names()]
    if unknown:
        raise ValueError(
            f"Unknown tool(s) {unknown}. Available tools: "
            f"{', '.join(_available_tool_names())}"
        )


def _validate_linked_profiles(manager: ProfileManager, linked: List[str]) -> None:
    """
    Validate the names of the profiles linked from this profile.

    Args:
        manager: Project ProfileManager.
        linked: Names of the profiles to link.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If any linked profile does not exist.
    """
    available = sorted({p.name for p in manager.list_all_profiles() if p and p.name})
    unknown = [name for name in linked if name not in available]
    if unknown:
        raise ValueError(
            f"Unknown linked profile(s) {unknown}. Available profiles: "
            f"{', '.join(available)}"
        )


def _validate_content(content: Optional[str]) -> List[str]:
    """
    Validate the Markdown content of a profile.

    Args:
        content: Proposed content.

    Returns:
        Warnings about the content.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If the content is empty.
    """
    if content is None or not content.strip():
        raise ValueError(
            "content is required: it is the profile's instructions (.md file)"
        )
    if len(content) > MAX_CONTENT_WARNING_CHARS:
        return [
            f"content has {len(content)} characters; it is injected into every "
            "chat where the profile is active. Consider trimming it."
        ]
    return []


def _resolve_target_name(profile_name: Optional[str], name: Optional[str]) -> str:
    """
    Resolve the profile a write targets, rejecting contradictory arguments.

    ``profile_name`` identifies the profile being read/updated/deleted while
    ``name`` is the field value of the definition; both are accepted for the
    same purpose so the model does not have to guess which one to use.

    Args:
        profile_name: Explicit target profile name.
        name: Profile name field.

    Returns:
        The validated profile name.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If both are provided and differ.
    """
    if profile_name and name and profile_name.strip() != name.strip():
        raise ValueError(
            f"Conflicting names: profile_name={profile_name!r} but name={name!r}"
        )
    return _validate_profile_name(profile_name or name or "")


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Actions
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def _action_list(
    manager: ProfileManager,
    category: Optional[str] = None,
    query: Optional[str] = None,
    include_inherited: bool = False,
) -> ToolResponse:
    """
    List profiles, optionally filtered.

    Args:
        manager: Project ProfileManager.
        category: Only profiles of this category.
        query: Case-insensitive substring matched against the name, the
            description and the tags.
        include_inherited: Include profiles inherited from parent projects and
            the built-in set (read-only).

    Returns:
        ToolResponse with the table (user) and the data (model).
    """
    profiles = (
        [p for p in manager.list_all_profiles() if p and p.name]
        if include_inherited
        else _project_profiles(manager)
    )

    if category:
        wanted = category.strip().lower()
        profiles = [p for p in profiles if (p.category or "").lower() == wanted]

    if query:
        needle = query.strip().lower()
        profiles = [
            p for p in profiles
            if needle in (p.name or "").lower()
            or needle in (p.description or "").lower()
            or any(needle in tag.lower() for tag in (p.tags or []))
        ]

    scope = "project + inherited" if include_inherited else "project"
    if not profiles:
        return ToolResponse(
            user_response=f"✓ No profiles found ({scope} scope)",
            llm_response=f"No profiles found (scope={scope}).",
        )

    user_response = "\n".join([
        _format_profiles_table(profiles),
        "",
        f"Scope: **{scope}**. Editable profiles live in "
        f"`{_relative_to_project(manager.settings, manager.profiles_path)}/`.",
    ])

    llm_response = json.dumps(
        {
            "scope": scope,
            "count": len(profiles),
            "profiles": [_profile_definition(p) for p in profiles],
        },
        indent=2,
    )
    logger.info("profile_management: listed %d profile(s) (%s)", len(profiles), scope)
    return ToolResponse(user_response=user_response, llm_response=llm_response)


def _action_get(manager: ProfileManager, name: str) -> ToolResponse:
    """
    Return the definition and the content of one profile.

    Args:
        manager: Project ProfileManager.
        name: Exact profile name.

    Returns:
        ToolResponse with the JSON definition and the Markdown content.
    """
    profile = _find_project_profile(manager, name)
    editable = profile is not None
    if profile is None:
        profile = _find_any_profile(manager, name)
    if profile is None:
        return ToolResponse(
            user_response=f"❌ Profile `{name}` not found",
            llm_response=(
                f"Profile '{name}' not found. Use action='list' "
                "(include_inherited=true) to see the available profiles."
            ),
        )

    paths = _profile_paths(manager, name)
    content_path = _relative_to_project(manager.settings, paths["content"])
    origin = "project" if editable else "inherited (read-only)"

    user_response = "\n".join([
        f"### Profile `{profile.name}`",
        f"> Origin: **{origin}** — definition: "
        f"`{_relative_to_project(manager.settings, profile.path)}`",
        "",
        "```json",
        json.dumps(_profile_definition(profile), indent=2),
        "```",
        "",
        f"**Content** (`{content_path}`)",
        "",
        "```markdown",
        profile.content or "",
        "```",
    ])

    llm_response = json.dumps(
        {
            **_profile_definition(profile, include_content=True),
            "editable": editable,
            "content_path": content_path,
        },
        indent=2,
    )
    logger.info(
        "profile_management: read profile '%s' (editable=%s)", name, editable
    )
    return ToolResponse(user_response=user_response, llm_response=llm_response)


def _action_create(
    manager: ProfileManager,
    name: str,
    description: Optional[str] = None,
    category: Optional[str] = None,
    content: Optional[str] = None,
    file_match: Optional[str] = None,
    profiles: Optional[List[str]] = None,
    tools: Optional[List[str]] = None,
    tags: Optional[List[str]] = None,
    llm_model: Optional[str] = None,
    use_knowledge: Optional[bool] = None,
    chat_mode: Optional[str] = None,
    avatar: Optional[str] = None,
    url: Optional[str] = None,
    api_settings: Optional[Dict[str, Any]] = None,
) -> ToolResponse:
    """
    Create a new profile (both files) in the project.

    Args:
        manager: Project ProfileManager.
        name: Profile name (folder name, validated).
        description: When to use the profile (1-3 sentences).
        category: One of :data:`PROFILE_CATEGORIES`.
        content: Markdown instructions (required).
        file_match: Optional regex matched against file paths.
        profiles: Optional names of linked profiles.
        tools: Optional tool names granted to the profile.
        tags: Optional discovery tags.
        llm_model: Optional model override.
        use_knowledge: Whether knowledge context is injected.
        chat_mode: Optional chat mode restriction.
        avatar: Optional avatar URL.
        url: Optional documentation URL.
        api_settings: Optional ``{active, model_name, description}``.

    Returns:
        ToolResponse describing the created profile.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If the profile already exists or a field is invalid.
    """
    existing = _find_any_profile(manager, name)
    if existing:
        raise ValueError(
            f"Profile '{name}' already exists at "
            f"'{_relative_to_project(manager.settings, existing.path)}'. "
            "Use action='update' to modify it."
        )

    category = _validate_category(category or DEFAULT_CATEGORY)
    warnings: List[str] = []
    warnings.extend(_validate_content(content))
    warnings.extend(_validate_file_match(file_match or ""))
    profiles = list(profiles or [])
    tools = list(tools or [])
    _validate_linked_profiles(manager, profiles)
    _validate_tools(tools)
    if not description:
        warnings.append(
            "description is empty: the profile card and the @mention picker will "
            "not explain when to use the profile."
        )

    profile = Profile(
        name=name,
        description=description or "",
        category=category,
        content=content,
        file_match=file_match or "",
        profiles=profiles,
        tools=tools,
        tags=list(tags or []),
        llm_model=llm_model or "",
        use_knowledge=True if use_knowledge is None else use_knowledge,
        chat_mode=chat_mode,
        avatar=avatar or "",
        url=url or "",
        api_settings=ProfileApiSettings(**(api_settings or {})),
        project_id=manager.settings.project_id,
    )
    profile.path = _profile_paths(manager, name)["profile"]

    manager.save_profile(profile)
    _notify(manager.settings, f"Profile '{name}' created")

    logger.info("profile_management: created profile '%s'", name)
    return _write_response(
        settings=manager.settings,
        profile=profile,
        manager=manager,
        title=f"Profile created: `{name}`",
        warnings=warnings,
    )


def _action_update(
    manager: ProfileManager,
    name: str,
    description: Optional[str] = None,
    category: Optional[str] = None,
    content: Optional[str] = None,
    file_match: Optional[str] = None,
    profiles: Optional[List[str]] = None,
    tools: Optional[List[str]] = None,
    tags: Optional[List[str]] = None,
    llm_model: Optional[str] = None,
    use_knowledge: Optional[bool] = None,
    chat_mode: Optional[str] = None,
    avatar: Optional[str] = None,
    url: Optional[str] = None,
    api_settings: Optional[Dict[str, Any]] = None,
) -> ToolResponse:
    """
    Update an existing project profile, merging the provided fields.

    Fields left as ``None`` keep their current value, so a partial update never
    wipes the rest of the definition or the Markdown content.

    Args:
        manager: Project ProfileManager.
        name: Exact name of the profile to update.
        description: New description.
        category: New category.
        content: New Markdown instructions (replaces the whole file).
        file_match: New ``file_match`` regex (``""`` clears it).
        profiles: New linked profile names (replaces the list).
        tools: New tool names (replaces the list).
        tags: New tags (replaces the list).
        llm_model: New model override (``""`` inherits the project model).
        use_knowledge: New knowledge flag.
        chat_mode: New chat mode restriction.
        avatar: New avatar URL.
        url: New documentation URL.
        api_settings: New ``{active, model_name, description}``.

    Returns:
        ToolResponse describing the updated profile.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If the profile does not exist in this project or a field is
            invalid.
    """
    existing = _find_project_profile(manager, name)
    if existing is None:
        other = _find_any_profile(manager, name)
        if other:
            raise ValueError(
                f"Profile '{name}' is inherited from "
                f"'{_relative_to_project(manager.settings, other.path)}' and is "
                "read-only. Create a project profile with the same name to "
                "override it (action='create')."
            )
        raise ValueError(
            f"Profile '{name}' does not exist in this project. "
            "Use action='create' to create it."
        )

    warnings: List[str] = []
    overrides: Dict[str, Any] = {}

    if description is not None:
        overrides["description"] = description
    if category is not None:
        overrides["category"] = _validate_category(category)
    if content is not None:
        warnings.extend(_validate_content(content))
        overrides["content"] = content
    if file_match is not None:
        warnings.extend(_validate_file_match(file_match))
        overrides["file_match"] = file_match
    if profiles is not None:
        _validate_linked_profiles(manager, list(profiles))
        overrides["profiles"] = list(profiles)
    if tools is not None:
        _validate_tools(list(tools))
        overrides["tools"] = list(tools)
    if tags is not None:
        overrides["tags"] = list(tags)
    if llm_model is not None:
        overrides["llm_model"] = llm_model
    if use_knowledge is not None:
        overrides["use_knowledge"] = use_knowledge
    if chat_mode is not None:
        overrides["chat_mode"] = chat_mode or None
    if avatar is not None:
        overrides["avatar"] = avatar
    if url is not None:
        overrides["url"] = url
    if api_settings is not None:
        overrides["api_settings"] = ProfileApiSettings(**api_settings)

    if not overrides:
        raise ValueError(
            "Nothing to update: provide at least one field "
            "(description, category, content, file_match, profiles, tools, tags, ...)"
        )

    profile = existing.model_copy(update=overrides)
    profile.name = name
    profile.path = _profile_paths(manager, name)["profile"]
    profile.project_id = manager.settings.project_id

    manager.save_profile(profile)
    _notify(manager.settings, f"Profile '{name}' updated")

    logger.info(
        "profile_management: updated profile '%s' (fields=%s)",
        name,
        ", ".join(sorted(overrides.keys())),
    )
    return _write_response(
        settings=manager.settings,
        profile=profile,
        manager=manager,
        title=f"Profile updated: `{name}`",
        warnings=warnings,
        changed_fields=sorted(overrides.keys()),
    )


def _action_delete(manager: ProfileManager, name: str) -> ToolResponse:
    """
    Delete a project profile (both files and its folder).

    Args:
        manager: Project ProfileManager.
        name: Exact name of the profile to delete.

    Returns:
        ToolResponse confirming the deletion.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If the profile is not owned by this project.
    """
    existing = _find_project_profile(manager, name)
    if existing is None:
        other = _find_any_profile(manager, name)
        if other:
            raise ValueError(
                f"Profile '{name}' is inherited from "
                f"'{_relative_to_project(manager.settings, other.path)}' and "
                "cannot be deleted from this project."
            )
        raise ValueError(f"Profile '{name}' does not exist in this project.")

    # Profiles linked from other definitions would be left dangling: report it
    # so the user can fix the references, but do not block the deletion.
    referenced_by = [
        p.name for p in _project_profiles(manager)
        if p.name != name and name in (p.profiles or [])
    ]

    paths = _profile_paths(manager, name)
    manager.delete_profile(name)
    _notify(manager.settings, f"Profile '{name}' deleted")

    logger.info("profile_management: deleted profile '%s'", name)

    user_lines = [
        f"### Profile deleted: `{name}`",
        "",
        f"- Folder removed: `{_relative_to_project(manager.settings, paths['folder'])}`",
    ]
    if referenced_by:
        user_lines.extend([
            "",
            f"> ⚠️ Still linked from: {', '.join(f'`{p}`' for p in referenced_by)}. "
            "Those links now point to a missing profile.",
        ])

    return ToolResponse(
        user_response="\n".join(user_lines),
        llm_response=json.dumps(
            {
                "deleted": name,
                "folder": _relative_to_project(manager.settings, paths["folder"]),
                "referenced_by": referenced_by,
            },
            indent=2,
        ),
    )


def _write_response(
    settings: CODXJuniorSettings,
    profile: Profile,
    manager: ProfileManager,
    title: str,
    warnings: Optional[List[str]] = None,
    changed_fields: Optional[List[str]] = None,
) -> ToolResponse:
    """
    Build the response shared by ``create`` and ``update``.

    Args:
        settings: Project settings.
        profile: The persisted profile.
        manager: Project ProfileManager.
        title: Heading of the user-facing block.
        warnings: Non-fatal problems found while validating.
        changed_fields: Fields modified by an update (``None`` on create).

    Returns:
        ToolResponse with the saved paths and the resulting definition.
    """
    paths = _profile_paths(manager, profile.name)
    definition_path = _relative_to_project(settings, paths["profile"])
    content_path = _relative_to_project(settings, paths["content"])

    lines = [
        f"### {title}",
        "",
        f"- Definition: `{definition_path}`",
        f"- Content: `{content_path}`",
        f"- Category: `{profile.category or '-'}` | "
        f"file_match: `{profile.file_match or 'none'}`",
        f"- Links: profiles `{', '.join(profile.profiles or []) or 'none'}` | "
        f"tools `{', '.join(profile.tools or []) or 'none'}`",
    ]
    if changed_fields:
        lines.append(f"- Changed: {', '.join(changed_fields)}")
    if warnings:
        lines.extend(["", "> ⚠️ " + "\n> ⚠️ ".join(warnings)])
    lines.extend([
        "",
        "Reload the profiles list to see the change in the UI.",
    ])

    llm_response = json.dumps(
        {
            "saved": profile.name,
            "definition_path": definition_path,
            "content_path": content_path,
            "changed_fields": changed_fields or [],
            "warnings": warnings or [],
            "profile": _profile_definition(profile),
        },
        indent=2,
    )
    return ToolResponse(
        user_response="\n".join(lines),
        llm_response=llm_response,
    )

def profile_management(
    action: str,
    profile_name: Optional[str] = None,
    name: Optional[str] = None,
    description: Optional[str] = None,
    category: Optional[str] = None,
    content: Optional[str] = None,
    file_match: Optional[str] = None,
    profiles: Optional[List[str]] = None,
    tools: Optional[List[str]] = None,
    tags: Optional[List[str]] = None,
    llm_model: Optional[str] = None,
    use_knowledge: Optional[bool] = None,
    chat_mode: Optional[str] = None,
    avatar: Optional[str] = None,
    url: Optional[str] = None,
    api_settings: Optional[Dict[str, Any]] = None,
    query: Optional[str] = None,
    include_inherited: bool = False,
    **kwargs,
) -> ToolResponse:
    """
    Unified CRUD tool for project profiles.

    Each profile is stored as two files inside ``.codx/profiles/<Name>/``:
    ``<Name>.profile`` (the JSON definition) and ``<Name>.md`` (the Markdown
    instructions). Both files are written together by ``ProfileManager``, so a
    profile is never left half-saved.

    Actions:
        - ``list``: profiles of the project (optional ``category``/``query``
          filters). ``include_inherited=True`` adds the read-only profiles
          inherited from parent projects and the built-in set.
        - ``get``: full definition (JSON) plus content (Markdown) of one
          profile.
        - ``create``: creates a new profile. Fails if the name already exists.
          ``content`` is required.
        - ``update``: merges the provided fields into an existing project
          profile; omitted fields keep their value.
        - ``delete``: removes the profile folder of a project profile.

    Writes always target the active project's ``.codx/profiles`` folder:
    inherited and built-in profiles are read-only.

    Args:
        action: One of :data:`VALID_ACTIONS`.
        profile_name: Target profile name (``get``/``update``/``delete``), also
            accepted on ``create``. On ``create`` it is optional when ``name``
            is provided.
        name: Profile name as a definition field (alias of ``profile_name`` for
            create/update).
        description: When to use the profile (1-3 sentences).
        category: One of ``assistant``, ``chat``, ``agent``, ``file``,
            ``project``. Defaults to ``assistant`` on create.
        content: Markdown instructions. Required on ``create``; replaces the
            whole content file on ``update``.
        file_match: Regex matched against file paths to auto-attach the
            profile. Empty string disables it.
        profiles: Names of the profiles to link (their content is injected when
            this profile runs).
        tools: Names of the tools granted to the profile. Must exist in the
            tool registry.
        tags: Discovery tags.
        llm_model: Model override (empty inherits the project/default model).
        use_knowledge: Whether knowledge context is injected.
        chat_mode: Chat mode restriction (e.g. ``task``).
        avatar: Avatar URL.
        url: Documentation URL.
        api_settings: ``{active, model_name, description}`` to expose the
            profile through the LLM API.
        query: ``list`` only. Case-insensitive filter on name, description and
            tags.
        include_inherited: ``list`` only. Include read-only inherited profiles.
        **kwargs: Internal. Injected by the agent runtime: ``settings``.

    Returns:
        ToolResponse: ``user_response`` for the chat, ``llm_response`` with the
        resulting definition for the model.

    Raises:
        Exception: If the project settings are missing.

    Example:
        >>> profile_management("list", category="assistant")
        # Lists every assistant profile of the project
        >>> profile_management("get", profile_name="TeamManager")
        # Shows the definition and the instructions
        >>> profile_management(
        ...     "create",
        ...     profile_name="Reviewer",
        ...     description="Reviews diffs for correctness and security.",
        ...     category="assistant",
        ...     content="# Reviewer Profile\\n\\n## Role\\n...",
        ...     tags=["code-review"],
        ... )
        # Creates .codx/profiles/Reviewer/Reviewer.profile + Reviewer.md
        >>> profile_management("update", profile_name="Reviewer", file_match=r"\\\\.diff$")
        # Updates only the file_match field
        >>> profile_management("delete", profile_name="Reviewer")
        # Removes the profile folder
    """
    settings: CODXJuniorSettings = kwargs.get("settings")
    if not settings:
        raise Exception("Invalid project settings")

    action = (action or "").strip().lower()
    if action not in VALID_ACTIONS:
        return ToolResponse(
            user_response=(
                f"❌ Invalid action `{action}`. Valid actions: "
                f"{', '.join(VALID_ACTIONS)}"
            ),
            llm_response=(
                f"Invalid action '{action}'. Valid actions: "
                f"{', '.join(VALID_ACTIONS)}"
            ),
        )

    manager = _get_profile_manager(settings)

    try:
        if action == "list":
            return _action_list(
                manager=manager,
                category=category,
                query=query,
                include_inherited=include_inherited,
            )

        if action == "get":
            return _action_get(
                manager=manager,
                name=_resolve_target_name(profile_name=profile_name, name=name),
            )

        if action == "create":
            return _action_create(
                manager=manager,
                name=_resolve_target_name(profile_name=profile_name, name=name),
                description=description,
                category=category,
                content=content,
                file_match=file_match,
                profiles=profiles,
                tools=tools,
                tags=tags,
                llm_model=llm_model,
                use_knowledge=use_knowledge,
                chat_mode=chat_mode,
                avatar=avatar,
                url=url,
                api_settings=api_settings,
            )

        if action == "update":
            return _action_update(
                manager=manager,
                name=_resolve_target_name(profile_name=profile_name, name=name),
                description=description,
                category=category,
                content=content,
                file_match=file_match,
                profiles=profiles,
                tools=tools,
                tags=tags,
                llm_model=llm_model,
                use_knowledge=use_knowledge,
                chat_mode=chat_mode,
                avatar=avatar,
                url=url,
                api_settings=api_settings,
            )

        return _action_delete(
            manager=manager,
            name=_resolve_target_name(profile_name=profile_name, name=name),
        )

    except ValueError as ex:
        # Validation errors are expected (typos, missing confirmation): report
        # them so the model can correct the call instead of crashing the run.
        logger.warning("profile_management(%s): %s", action, ex)
        return ToolResponse(
            user_response=f"❌ {ex}",
            llm_response=f"profile_management action '{action}' failed: {ex}",
        )
    except Exception as ex:
        logger.exception("profile_management(%s): unexpected error", action)
        return ToolResponse(
            user_response=f"❌ Error: {ex}",
            llm_response=f"profile_management action '{action}' failed: {ex}",
        )

## Usage

| Action | Call | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| Read | `profile_management("list")` | Markdown table of project profiles |
| Read | `profile_management("get", profile_name="TeamManager")` | JSON definition + `.md` content |
| Create | `profile_management("create", profile_name="Reviewer", category="assistant", description="…", content="# Reviewer…")` | Writes `.codx/profiles/Reviewer/Reviewer.profile` + `Reviewer.md` |
| Update | `profile_management("update", profile_name="Reviewer", file_match="\\.diff$")` | Merges only `file_match` |
| Delete | `profile_management("delete", profile_name="Reviewer")` | Removes the folder, warns on dangling links |

## Guardrails to avoid

- ❌ **Silent overwrite** — `create` fails on an existing name; `update` fails on a missing one. Renaming is `create` + `delete`, so both files always move together.
- ❌ **Hijacking chats via `file_match`** — broad patterns (`.*`, `.+`) are accepted but reported back as a warning in the response.
- ❌ **Breaking `@mentions`** — names are validated against `^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9_\-\.]*$`; spaces or slashes would make the profile unreferenceable and could escape the profiles folder.

Unified logging, event emission and cancellation for agent runs.
Wraps openai_ai without modifying it: openai_ai's stream/tool callbacks
are adapted onto AgentRunContext.

import json
import logging
import threading
import time
import uuid
from contextlib import contextmanager
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from enum import Enum
from typing import Any, Callable, Iterable, Iterator

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# Errors
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
class AgentCancelled(Exception):
    """Raised at checkpoints when the run has been cancelled."""


class InsufficientFundsError(Exception):
    """Raised by the wallet pre-flight check."""


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# Cancellation
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
class CancellationToken:
    """Thread-safe cancellation token. cancel() may be called from any thread
    (e.g. a Socket.IO 'stop' handler) while the agent loop runs elsewhere."""

    def __init__(self):
        self._event = threading.Event()
        self.reason: str | None = None

    def cancel(self, reason: str = "user_requested"):
        self.reason = reason
        self._event.set()

    @property
    def cancelled(self) -> bool:
        return self._event.is_set()

    def raise_if_cancelled(self):
        if self._event.is_set():
            raise AgentCancelled(self.reason or "cancelled")


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# Events
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
class AgentEventType(str, Enum):
    RUN_START = "run_start"
    RUN_END = "run_end"
    RUN_ERROR = "run_error"
    RUN_CANCELLED = "run_cancelled"
    LLM_REQUEST = "llm_request"
    LLM_CHUNK = "llm_chunk"
    LLM_USAGE = "llm_usage"
    TOOL_START = "tool_start"
    TOOL_END = "tool_end"
    TOOL_ERROR = "tool_error"
    TOOL_LOGS = "tool_logs"
    WALLET_CHECK = "wallet_check"


@dataclass
class AgentEvent:
    type: AgentEventType
    run_id: str
    project_id: str
    payload: dict = field(default_factory=dict)
    ts: float = field(default_factory=time.time)

    def to_dict(self) -> dict:
        return {"type": self.type.value, "run_id": self.run_id,
                "project_id": self.project_id, "ts": self.ts, **self.payload}


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# Analytics (tokens & tools) — fed automatically by emit()
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
@dataclass
class RunAnalytics:
    prompt_tokens: int = 0
    completion_tokens: int = 0
    tool_calls: dict = field(default_factory=dict)   # name -> {count, errors, total_ms}

    def on_event(self, event: AgentEvent):
        p = event.payload
        if event.type == AgentEventType.LLM_USAGE:
            self.prompt_tokens += p.get("prompt_tokens", 0)
            self.completion_tokens += p.get("completion_tokens", 0)
        elif event.type in (AgentEventType.TOOL_END, AgentEventType.TOOL_ERROR):
            stats = self.tool_calls.setdefault(
                p.get("tool", "unknown"), {"count": 0, "errors": 0, "total_ms": 0.0})
            stats["count"] += 1
            stats["total_ms"] += p.get("duration_ms", 0.0)
            if event.type == AgentEventType.TOOL_ERROR:
                stats["errors"] += 1

    def summary(self) -> dict:
        return {"prompt_tokens": self.prompt_tokens,
                "completion_tokens": self.completion_tokens,
                "total_tokens": self.prompt_tokens + self.completion_tokens,
                "tools": self.tool_calls}

"""
SmolAgent: a small, async-only OpenAI chat agent.

Compared to the removed :class:`codx.junior.ai.openai_ai.OpenAI_AI`, this
implementation:
    * exposes a single async ``chat()`` method (no sync variant),
    * uses an **iterative** tool loop instead of recursion,
    * delegates loop protection to :class:`LoopGuard`,
    * delegates logging, event emission and cancellation to
      :class:`engine.agent_runtime.AgentRunContext`,
    * keeps streaming, callbacks, cancellation and analytics.
    * caches tool results per conversation to avoid re-execution.
    * returns a typed :class:`AgentRunResult` (no untyped ``additional_kwargs``).

Tool events (``TOOL_START`` / ``TOOL_END`` / ``TOOL_ERROR`` / ``TOOL_LOGS``) carry the
``tool_call_id``, the parsed JSON request args and a truncated result preview
so listeners (e.g. the ChatEventBridge) can surface tool executions as chat
messages in real time. ``TOOL_END`` additionally carries the dual-response tool's
user-facing ``output`` (see Message Structure below). Tool logs are emitted for
forensic audit trail.

Loop-Limit Handling
When :class:`LoopGuard` stops the run (max rounds, max tool calls or stuck
loop), the run is **not** aborted. Instead the tool-usage value is summarised
by the project's knowledge/RAG model and appended to the assistant answer, so
the findings survive in the persisted message and the next iteration can
continue without re-running the same tools. The summary request is
best-effort, does not count towards the loop limits, and its token usage is
recorded separately with the ``tool-analysis`` tag.

Cost-Limit Handling
Every round (iteration) computes its cost in cxjcoins from the provider usage
and the model price settings, accumulates it into the chat total and reports it
on the returned :class:`AgentRunResult` (``result.cost``). Tools that report
their own cost through :attr:`ToolResponse.cost` are summed into both the
per-run total and the chat total. The chat total is seeded from ``Chat.cost``
(the accumulated, deletion-safe value maintained by ChatManager) so the budget
applies to the whole chat and is not reset when messages are deleted. When the
chat reaches its estimated cost (``Chat.estimation_cost``), the run stops
gracefully — before executing further tools — to keep the chat within budget.

Message Structure
A single final assistant message is always produced. Its ``content`` holds only
the model's own text: reasoning emitted between tool rounds plus the final
answer. Tool output is NO LONGER merged into the message content. For
dual-response tools, ``ToolResponse.user_response`` is emitted on the ``TOOL_END``
event and attached to the response message as a collapsible property
(``ToolEvent.output``), so the client decides how to render it (collapsed or
hidden) and the chat stays clean.

Vision API Support
Binary files (PDFs, images) are passed as vision content when models support it.
The content is merged into the final user message to enable vision-capable models
to process images and documents alongside text.

Error Visibility
Every AI provider interaction (the completion request, the streaming of its
response and the tool-usage summary request) is guarded so failures are logged
VERBATIM: phase, model, provider, endpoint, whether an API key is configured,
message/tool counts, request/chat/run identifiers, HTTP status, provider
``code``/``param``/``request_id``, provider request-id header, response body
(truncated) and the chained root cause (``httpx.ConnectError``, DNS, TLS,
timeout, proxy, ...) — always followed by a full traceback. A short Markdown
notice with the same details is also streamed to the client, because previously
a failed connection surfaced as nothing more than the provider's generic
``"Connection error."`` string in both the logs and the chat.

    if ignore_list is None:

## 1. Review & Understand the Task

- **Goal:** add tools that manage **teams** in codx-junior (plural "tools").
- **Constraint discovered:** *no team concept exists anywhere* in the codebase. The closest primitives are **profiles** (`ProfileManager`, `.codx/profiles/<Name>/<Name>.profile` + `.md`) and the **`TeamManager` profile** created in the previous turn (a *profile builder* — it composes profiles, not teams).
- Therefore a team must be defined and persisted here, following the existing conventions: manager class + pydantic model + `tools/*.py` + registration in `TOOLS`.

### Findings that drive the design

| Piece | Location | Consequence |
|---|---|---|
| Profile storage: folder + `<Name>.profile` (JSON) + `<Name>.md` (content) | `profiles/profile_manager.py` | Teams mirror this layout: `.codx/teams/<Name>/<Name>.team` + `<Name>.md` |
| `Profile.profiles` = linked profile names, expanded recursively by `get_all_linked_profiles` | `profile_manager.py` | A team **references** profiles; it must not copy them |

| Tool | Actions | Purpose |
|---|---|---|

"""
Team models for codx-junior.

A **team** is a named group of profiles that work together on one capability:
a lead profile plus the profiles that cover the different responsibilities.

Teams are the *composition* layer on top of profiles: a team never stores the
instructions of its members, it only references their names. The instructions
are resolved by
:class:`~codx.junior.teams.team_manager.TeamManager` when the team is used, so
a team can never drift from the profile it composes.

Storage layout (one folder per team)::

    .codx/teams/<Name>/<Name>.team   # JSON definition (this model)
    .codx/teams/<Name>/<Name>.md     # Markdown charter (``content``)

The layout mirrors ``.codx/profiles`` on purpose: same two files, same
folder-name-equals-name invariant.

Made with ❤️ by codx-junior
"""

from datetime import datetime
from typing import List, Optional

from pydantic import BaseModel, Field


class TeamMember(BaseModel):
    """
    One profile taking part in a team.

    The member is identified by ``profile`` (the profile **name**), and adds
    the part that only makes sense inside the team: the role and the
    responsibility this profile owns.

    Attributes:
        profile: Profile name (as used by ``@mentions``).
        role: Short role inside the team (``lead``, ``backend``, ``reviewer``...).
        responsibility: One line describing what this member owns.
        order: Sort order when composing the team instructions.
    """

    profile: str = Field(default="", description="Name of the profile this member plays")
    role: str = Field(default="", description="Role inside the team, e.g. 'backend'")
    responsibility: str = Field(
        default="",
        description="One line: what this member owns inside the team",
    )
    order: int = Field(
        default=0,
        description="Order used when composing the team instructions",
    )


class Team(BaseModel):
    """
    A group of profiles working together under a lead.

    Attributes:
        name: Team identity. Also the folder name and the ``@mention``, so it
            must be mention-safe (letters, digits, ``_``, ``-``, ``.``).
        description: When to use the team, in 1-3 sentences.
        goal: The outcome the team is responsible for.
        avatar: Avatar URL shown in the UI.
